audits.title: A Retrospective Audit of Compliance with International Standards in Colorectal Cancer Pathology Reporting in a National Referral Hospital in Tanzania
audits.standard: International Collaboration on Cancer Reporting (ICCR) colorectal cancer reporting checklist
audits.setting: Central Pathology Laboratory, Muhimbili National Hospital

cycle1.result: Clinical impression 83.6%, type of colectomy 91.3%, neoadjuvant history 57.4%, intraoperative tumour extent 50.8%. Lymph node harvesting adequate in 44.8%, radial margin sampling 45.9%. Reports: histologic subtype and extension 92.3%, lymph node status 67.2%, pathological staging 71%, radial margin status 45.9%.

audits.intervention: Recommended adoption of ICCR synoptic reporting and stronger multidisciplinary communication.
audits.other_findings: Detailed intraoperative findings were associated with better grossing and reporting quality.
audits.citation: Shomvi A, Vuhahula E, Ali F, Matiku S, Shaban I, Jaka H, et al.. A Retrospective Audit of Compliance with International Standards in Colorectal Cancer Pathology Reporting in a National Referral Hospital in Tanzania. . 2026. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-4795221/v1.

audits.title: Pathology reporting of rectal cancer: a national audit.
audits.standard: Predefined proforma for rectal cancer histopathology reports
audits.setting: Reports submitted to the National Cancer Registry

cycle1.result: Multiple staging systems in 40% of reports; no stage in 31%; circumferential margin involvement recorded in 63%.

audits.other_findings: No significant differences between teaching, non-teaching and private laboratories.
audits.citation: Keating J, Lolohea S, Kenwright D. Pathology reporting of rectal cancer: a national audit. N Z Med J. 2003;116(1178):U514. PMID: 12897882.

audits.title: Quality and completeness of histopathology reports of rectal cancer resections. Results of an audit in Brittany.
audits.standard: French 1998 guidelines for pathology reports of rectal cancer resections (at least 8 lymph nodes examined)

cycle1.result: Number of nodes examined in 204 (84%); at least 8 nodes in 53.4%; circumferential margin recorded in 27%; pTNM staging in 67%.

audits.other_findings: Venous/lymphatic invasion recorded in 34% and neural invasion in 18%.
audits.citation: Eon Y, Le Douy JY, Lamer B, Battini J, Bretagne JF. Quality and completeness of histopathology reports of rectal cancer resections. Results of an audit in Brittany. Gastroenterol Clin Biol. 2006;30(2):235-240. doi:10.1016/s0399-8320(06)73159-1. PMID: 16565656.

audits.title: The quality of pathological reports of postoperative specimens in rectal cancer: an audit from the Mazovia region.
audits.standard: Pathology standards: mesorectal excision quality, circumferential resection margin and at least 12 lymph nodes
audits.setting: Rectal cancer patients from 19 hospitals referred to Maria Sklodowska-Curie Cancer Centre, Mazovia region

cycle1.result: Mesorectal excision quality reported in 14%; CRM measured in 57%; median lymph nodes retrieved 9 (range 0-36).

audits.other_findings: Authors call for national action and guidelines for pathologists.
audits.citation: Olszyna-Serementa M, Kołodziejczyk M, Sprawka A, Nasierowska-Guttmejer A, Bujko K. The quality of pathological reports of postoperative specimens in rectal cancer: an audit from the Mazovia region. Pol J Pathol. 2009;60(3):130-133. PMID: 20069506.

audits.title: Completeness of low anterior resection pathology report: a hospital-based audit with recommendations on improving reporting.
audits.standard: Royal College of Pathologists minimum data sets
audits.setting: Department of Pathology, Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Kochi

cycle1.result: 19% of reports satisfactory; CRM completeness statement in 30.5% (18/59); relation to peritoneal reflection in 25.4%.

audits.citation: Nambiar A, Vivek N, Bindu MR, Sudheer OV, Bai L. Completeness of low anterior resection pathology report: a hospital-based audit with recommendations on improving reporting. Indian J Cancer. 2010;47(2):156-159. doi:10.4103/0019-509x.63010. PMID: 20448379.

audits.title: A survey of reporting of colorectal cancer in Scotland: compliance with guidelines and effect of proforma reporting.
audits.standard: Royal College of Pathologists (2007) standards and NHS Quality Improvement Scotland standards
audits.setting: 10 Scottish health boards reporting colorectal cancer resections

cycle1.result: Only three units met RCPath standards for rectal cancer reporting; non-proforma units failed minimum standards for serosal involvement (6%) and EMVI (24%); rectal cases with mean node count of 12 or more 56% (non-proforma) vs 81% (proforma).

audits.other_findings: Rectal cancer reporting was generally worse than colonic; units using proformas were more likely to meet guidelines.
audits.citation: Woods YL, Mukhtar S, McClements P, Lang J, Steele RJ, Carey FA. A survey of reporting of colorectal cancer in Scotland: compliance with guidelines and effect of proforma reporting. J Clin Pathol. 2014;67(6):499-505. doi:10.1136/jclinpath-2013-202060. PMID: 24567415.

audits.title: Colorectal cancer pathology reporting: a regional audit.
audits.standard: Items previously agreed as desirable by pathologists in Wales, and minimum standards for patient management
audits.setting: 17 NHS histopathology laboratories in Wales (regional audit)

cycle1.result: Minimum standards met in 78% (969/1242) of colonic and 46.6% (579/1242) of rectal reports; all agreed items in 11.3% (140/1242) colonic and 4.0% (40/1242) rectal reports; circumferential margin stated in 51.5% (640/1242) of rectal reports; number of involved nodes in 30% (373/1242).

audits.other_findings: Notable variation between laboratories; template proforma reporting recommended.
audits.citation: Bull AD, Biffin AH, Mella J, Radcliffe AG, Stamatakis JD, Steele RJ, et al.. Colorectal cancer pathology reporting: a regional audit. J Clin Pathol. 1997;50(2):138-142. doi:10.1136/jcp.50.2.138. PMID: 9155695.
